message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy. The audited statements show total net sales of **$391,035M** (up 2% from $383,285M), operating income of **$123,216M** on a 46.2% gross margin, net income of **$93,736M**, diluted EPS of **$6.08**, and operating cash flow of **$118,254M** — a highly cash-generative franchise with $140.8B in unrestricted cash and marketable securities, even after a $10.2B one-time State Aid tax charge. I deliberately discounted two MD&A claims that conflict with the audited financials (a "41%" Services growth statement, versus the actual $96,169M vs $85,200M = +13%, and a "grow more than 25% in fiscal 2025" projection), relying instead on the audited statement figures. With the stock at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), that's ~36.6x FY24 EPS on a business still growing modestly with expanding Services mix. I placed one limit order: **buy 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75** (≈$9,801, under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total, and only 0.02% above the prevailing ask, well within the "close to market price" requirement); it filled at $222.75. No sales or withdrawals were made, the existing 100 MSFT shares were untouched, and $50,000 cash remains available for any further qualifying order today.
